title: Proof of the crossed-module structure
html: Proof. At each level n, the pair (\mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2), \mathcal{O}_M^{\times}) forms a crossed module [yekutieli2010]. The boundary map \partial \colon \mathcal{O}_M^{\times} \to \mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2) sends a unit a \in \mathcal{O}_M^{\times} to the central element a \cdot \mathbf{1} \in \mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2) via the central extension. The action of g \in \mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2) on a \in \mathcal{O}_M^{\times} is conjugation: g \cdot a = g a g^{-1}. This action is well-defined because \mathcal{O}_M^{\times} is central in the gerbe band, rendering the Peiffer identity \partial(a) \cdot b = a b a^{-1} automatic for the central extension. \square
